# Fire Water System Control Narrative: Module FW

**Document status:** Draft A, 2026-10-18. This draft is not yet approved by operations.
**Scope:** Site PLC/SCADA functions for FP-1, FP-2, JP-1, PT-601, LT-610 and the pump room temperature.

## 0. Corrections to the client draft

| ID | Client draft | Problem | Position in this narrative |
|---|---|---|---|
| C-1 | PLC starts fire pumps on low header pressure | The listed controllers FPC-1 and FPC-2 must start the pumps from their own pressure sensing (NFPA 20). A PLC in the start path adds a failure mode and sits outside the listing. | The PLC does not start FP-1 or FP-2. The PLC monitors only. FR-FW-001 |
| C-2 | PLC stops pumps after 10 min of recovered pressure | Stopping is a controller function. NFPA 20 allows automatic stop only for a pressure-started pump with a run-period timer. The required time can differ between diesel and electric controllers. | The PLC has no stop output to either pump. Both pumps stop manually at the controller. Auto-stop is an open item (OI-1). FR-FW-002 |
| C-3 | PLC trips FP-1 on low lube oil pressure and high coolant temperature | NFPA 20 requires a fire pump diesel to run through these conditions. Only overspeed may stop it, and the engine controller does that. A trip can remove the pump during a fire. | The PLC alarms low oil pressure and high coolant temperature. It never stops FP-1. FR-FW-003 |

Confirm the NFPA 20 edition and the AHJ requirements before approval (OI-1).

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

- FW keeps the fire water header pressurized and shows pump status to operators.
- JP-1 is the only pump the PLC commands. JP-1 is not a listed fire pump.
- FPC-1 and FPC-2 own all start, stop and engine-protection logic for FP-1 and FP-2.
- Upstream: fire water supply and the pump suction source. Downstream: the fire water header at PT-601.
- Fire alarm panel (FACP) signaling is separate from this PLC scope. See OI-4.
- Any safety instrumented function is outside this document. A SIS function would be in the SRS, per IEC 61511. None is assumed.

## 2. Equipment and tags

No instrument index was given. Tags marked * are proposed.

| Tag | Description | Signal to PLC |
|---|---|---|
| FP-1 | Diesel fire pump | Run (from FPC-1) |
| FPC-1* | Listed diesel controller | Run, fail to start, trouble group, engine alarms, power available |
| FP-2 | Electric fire pump | Run (from FPC-2) |
| FPC-2* | Listed electric controller | Run, fail to start, trouble group, power available |
| ATS-2* | Automatic transfer switch | Normal source, emergency source |
| JP-1 | Jockey pump | Run (PLC output and feedback) |
| PT-601 | Header pressure | 4-20 mA |
| LT-610 | FP-1 diesel fuel tank level | 4-20 mA |
| TT-620* | Pump room temperature | 4-20 mA |

- Wire controller signals as hardwired contacts. Use the fail-safe contact form so that a broken wire reads as abnormal. Confirm the contact form per controller (OI-5).
- Do not wire any PLC output to a start, stop or test input of FPC-1 or FPC-2.

## 3. States and transitions

| State | Entry permissive | Description | Exits | Initiator | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FW-00 Out of Service | JP-1 selector in OFF, or maintenance bypass set | JP-1 stopped. Monitoring and alarms stay active. | FW-01 | Operator | Manual |
| FW-01 Standby | JP-1 selector in AUTO, PT-601 good, no fire pump running | JP-1 maintains header pressure. | FW-02, FW-03, FW-00 | Auto / operator | Automatic |
| FW-02 Demand | FP-1 run or FP-2 run | JP-1 stopped and locked out. The PLC alarms and records the run. | FW-01 only after both pumps are stopped by hand and PT-601 is good | Operator | Manual stop at controller |
| FW-03 Degraded | Any controller trouble, fail to start, low fuel, or bad PT-601, with no pump running | JP-1 follows the rules of FR-FW-020. | FW-01 when all conditions clear and are acknowledged; FW-02 | Auto | Automatic |

Transitions to FW-02 do not need any permissive. A running fire pump always takes priority (FR-FW-004).

## 4. Regulatory control

No PID loops. JP-1 uses on/off control with hysteresis.

| Item | PV | Output | Action | Mode behavior |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| JP-1 pressure control | PT-601 | JP-1 run command | Start at the JP-1 start point. Stop at the JP-1 stop point. See SP-FW-01 and SP-FW-02. | AUTO as above. OFF holds JP-1 stopped. No cascade or override. |

## 5. Sequences

### 5.1 JP-1 start/stop (SqBC)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Wait in standby | PT-601 at or below SP-FW-01, JP-1 off time at least SP-FW-09, no fire pump running | none | none |
| 2 | Start JP-1 | JP-1 run feedback true | SP-FW-08 | Stop JP-1. Raise JP-1 fail-to-start alarm. Latch it. Reset by operator. |
| 3 | Run JP-1 | PT-601 at or above SP-FW-02 and run time at least SP-FW-10 | SP-FW-11 | Keep JP-1 running. Raise JP-1 long-run alarm (possible leak or demand). |
| 4 | Stop JP-1 | Run feedback false | SP-FW-08 | Raise JP-1 fail-to-stop alarm. |

### 5.2 Demand monitoring (no commands)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Detect low header | PT-601 below SP-FW-04 or SP-FW-03 | none | none |
| 2 | Check pump started | Matching pump run true | SP-FW-07 | Raise pump fail-to-start-on-demand alarm. Do not issue any command. |
| 3 | Latch run record | Any fire pump run true | none | Hold FW-02 until both pumps are off and the operator resets. |

## 6. Interlocks and permissives

No cause-and-effect chart was given. These rows are the full set for this module.

| Cause | Effect | Latched or auto-reset | Reset method |
|---|---|---|---|
| FP-1 run or FP-2 run | Stop JP-1. Inhibit JP-1 start. | Auto-reset | Both pumps off |
| JP-1 selector OFF | Stop JP-1 | Auto-reset | Selector to AUTO |
| PT-601 bad PV | Stop JP-1 | Auto-reset | PT-601 good for SP-FW-15 |
| JP-1 fail to start | Stop JP-1. Inhibit restart. | Latched | Operator reset |
| JP-1 overload trip | Stop JP-1 | Latched | Operator reset at the motor starter |
| FP-1 low oil, high coolant or any engine alarm | Alarm only. No effect on FP-1. | Auto-reset | Condition clears |

## 7. Alarms

No alarm database was given. Priorities are provisional. Alarm response text is in the SDS.

| Alarm | Trigger | Priority | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|
| FP-1 running | FPC-1 run | High | Confirm a real demand. Find the cause. Inform the fire team. |
| FP-2 running | FPC-2 run | High | Same as above. |
| FP-1 or FP-2 fail to start | Controller fail-to-start signal | High | Go to the pump room. Start the pump by hand at the controller. |
| Pump fail to start on demand | See 5.2, step 2 | High | Same as above. |
| FPC-1 or FPC-2 trouble | Trouble group | High | Inspect the controller. Repair before the next shift. |
| FP-2 on emergency source | ATS-2 emergency source true | High | Find the cause of the normal power loss. |
| FP-1 engine alarm (low oil, high coolant, other) | Signals from FPC-1 | High | Go to the pump room. Do not stop the engine. |
| Header pressure low | PT-601 below SP-FW-05 | High | Check for demand or a leak. |
| Header pressure high | PT-601 above SP-FW-06 | Medium | Check for a jockey or relief fault. |
| LT-610 low | Below SP-FW-12 | Medium | Refuel FP-1. |
| LT-610 low-low | Below SP-FW-13 | High | Refuel FP-1 now. |
| Pump room temperature low | Below SP-FW-14 | High | Check heaters. Engine start can fail when cold. |
| Pump room temperature high | Above SP-FW-16 | Medium | Check ventilation. |
| JP-1 fail to start, long run, overload | See 5.1 | Medium | Inspect JP-1. Check for header leaks. |
| PT-601, LT-610 or TT-620 bad PV | Signal outside SP-FW-17 range | Medium | Check the instrument. |

## 8. Abnormal handling

| Condition | Module response |
|---|---|
| PT-601 bad PV | Stop JP-1. Raise alarm. The fire pumps are not affected, because the controllers sense pressure themselves. |
| LT-610 or TT-620 bad PV | Raise alarm. Hold the last good value on the HMI, marked as bad. |
| Controller signal lost (wire break) | Read as abnormal. Raise the matching trouble alarm. |
| Network link lost to SCADA (if used) | The PLC keeps running local logic. SCADA marks all FW values as stale after SP-FW-18. |
| PLC power loss | JP-1 contactor de-energizes and JP-1 stops. FP-1 and FP-2 are not affected. |
| PLC restart | JP-1 stays stopped until PT-601 is good for SP-FW-15 and the selector is in AUTO. Pump run states are read from the controllers. The PLC does not assume them. |
| Fail positions | JP-1 fails stopped. The PLC controls no valves. |

## 9. Operator interface

- **See:** pump run, fail to start, controller trouble, engine alarms, ATS source, PT-601 trend, LT-610, TT-620, JP-1 state, FW state.
- **Change:** JP-1 selector (OFF/AUTO), alarm acknowledge, alarm reset. No setpoint edits from SCADA for the fire pumps.
- **Not provided:** any start, stop or test command for FP-1 or FP-2. A remote start would use a listed remote start input on the controller (OI-2).
- **Prompts:** "Both fire pumps are stopped. Reset FW-02?"; "Reset JP-1 fail to start?"
- Operations signs off on states and prompts (OI-6).

## Requirements and test methods

| ID | Requirement | FAT/SAT test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-FW-001 | The PLC shall not have any output to start FP-1 or FP-2. | Inspect I/O list and wiring. Confirm no such output exists. |
| FR-FW-002 | The PLC shall not have any output to stop FP-1 or FP-2. Both pumps stop manually at the controller. | Same inspection. Run each pump and stop at the controller. |
| FR-FW-003 | The PLC shall alarm FP-1 engine conditions and shall not stop FP-1. | Simulate each engine alarm. Confirm alarm and no change to FP-1. |
| FR-FW-004 | FW shall enter FW-02 when FP-1 or FP-2 runs. | Simulate each run signal. |
| FR-FW-010 | JP-1 shall start at SP-FW-01 and stop at SP-FW-02. | Ramp PT-601 simulation up and down. |
| FR-FW-011 | JP-1 shall obey the minimum run and off times. | Cycle PT-601 quickly. Check the timers. |
| FR-FW-012 | JP-1 shall stop and be locked out while a fire pump runs. | Simulate FP-1, then FP-2, while JP-1 runs. |
| FR-FW-013 | JP-1 shall latch a fail-to-start alarm after the timeout. | Block the run feedback. |
| FR-FW-020 | In FW-03, JP-1 shall keep control unless PT-601 is bad, when it shall stop. | Fail PT-601. Simulate controller trouble. |
| FR-FW-030 | The PLC shall raise every alarm in section 7 at its setpoint. | Simulate each trigger. |
| FR-FW-040 | The PLC shall respond as in section 8 to bad PV, wire break, comms loss, power loss and restart. | Fault injection; power cycle. |
| FR-FW-041 | JP-1 shall fail stopped on PLC power loss. | Remove PLC power. |
